$comment: THE GUARD REGISTRY — every enforcement promise OneEngine makes.
`scripts/guards.test.mjs` reads this file. Four rules make it more than a
1. A `live` guard names an implementation AND a literal string that
implementation contains. Rename the assertion and the registry fails,
so a guard cannot quietly stop existing.
2. A `live` guard must actually RUN — reached by `pnpm engine:gate`,
`engine:test` or `engine:typecheck`. A check nobody invokes is no check.
A guard whose implementation is a `*.seen.test.*` file launches a
browser, so it runs in `pnpm engine:seen` and NOT in CI; it declares
`"lane": "seen"`, and the tag has to match the filename both ways.
3. Every guard names the DECISION it protects. A guard defending nothing
recorded is one whose reason is forgotten and which is then deleted as
noise by somebody who cannot see what it was for.
4. An `owed` guard names a stage, and a SHIPPED stage may owe nothing —
which is what makes `docs/stages.json` mean anything.
`fails` is a consequence in the world, never a restatement of the assertion:
"a tenant's records unreachable after a move", not "the key is wrong".

guards.becomes: elsewhere: the registry and the manifests, which is where a vocabulary entry is either used or is not, however a screen is expressed
guards.proves: placed by a declaration
guards.fails: a registry that grows entries nothing composes - the slot-to-prop join is asserted statically and no render ever makes it good, so the entry is correct on paper and draws an empty region the first time an app names it; thirteen charts and six list shapes were registered that way, chosen by listing what the design package exports rather than by counting what a product draws

guards.becomes: elsewhere: the import graph, which is where a file is reached or is not, whatever the product's browser half turns into
guards.proves: rendered by something
guards.fails: a hand-written screen left inside a product with its wiring already done - no route names it, no session map holds it and no harness photographs it, so every check here reports ok while it sits one import away from being live again; that is the shape somebody reaches for when a declaration will not say what they want, and 210 lines of it survived the surface being emptied

guards.proves: a binding reaches the prop it names
guards.fails: a binding that resolves and never arrives - a value read correctly out of the record and handed to a prop nothing reads, a format that never reaches a formatter so every price ships as a bare integer of minor units, a condition that draws a block it should have left out, and a split whose aside was left in the main column

guards.proves: file(s) swept, none deciding by the width of the window
guards.fails: a component that reflows on the viewport while sitting in a box the viewport knows nothing about - four columns drawn into 300 pixels on a 1440px monitor, every one of them a word per line, and the reverse where a list given the whole of a tablet stays a phone list; plus a container rule with no container over it, which resolves against whatever ancestor happens to be one and fires on somebody else's width; and an element carrying both the container declaration and the rule that queries it, which cannot query itself and so is inert at every width while typechecking and shipping its class

guards.becomes: elsewhere: this registry and the manifests behind it — the one guard whose subject is the port itself
guards.proves: every guard that sweeps a product says what its question becomes
guards.fails: a guard that narrows in silence as screens are ported - a `.tsx` question asked of a `body:` that cannot contain a className, a bare fetch or a catch that answers a failure with a fact, so the check goes unanswered rather than red and the corpus shrinks one screen at a time behind an unchanged `ok`; plus a refusal claimed as the replacement that the kernel does not emit or that no test asserts, and a bare `unrepresentable` with no clause saying what the grammar has no room for

guards.becomes: reads: it is the one guard whose subject is which screens are declarations

guards.fails: a product growing a hand-written screen on an afternoon nobody reviewed - every other check in this directory reads a .tsx and reports ok over it, so the arc loses ground behind a green run; plus an exemption that outlives its reason, either because the screen it names became a declaration and the entry stayed, or because it names a screen no product declares and covers nothing at all
